description: Standalone Kubernetes resource management desktop application with tree navigation and resource views.

tech_stack.notes: Use electron-vite for Electron + Vite integration. Tailwind v4 via @tailwindcss/vite plugin. shadcn/ui components copied into src/renderer/components/ui/. Main process handles kubeconfig and k8s API calls via IPC; renderer is the React UI.

architecture.main_process: Reads ~/.kube/config, creates k8s API clients, exposes IPC handlers for resource queries
architecture.renderer_process: React app with Tailwind layout: left tree view + right resource panel. shadcn/ui components for Table, Sheet, Badge, Collapsible.
architecture.ipc_pattern: renderer calls ipcRenderer.invoke('k8s:<resource>:<action>', ...args), main process returns serialized data

stories.title: Project scaffold with Electron + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn
stories.description: Initialize the project using the official electron-vite scaffold: run `npm create @quick-start/electron@latest . -- --template react-ts` in the project root (the dot targets the current directory). Then: (1) Install Tailwind CSS v4 via `npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite` and add the Vite plugin to electron.vite.config.ts renderer config. (2) Add `@import 'tailwindcss'` to src/renderer/assets/main.css. (3) Configure shadcn by creating components.json manually (do NOT run npx shadcn init as it misdetects the electron-vite structure). The components.json should set aliases pointing to src/renderer/. (4) Install shadcn peer deps: `npm install class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react @radix-ui/react-collapsible @radix-ui/react-slot`. (5) Install remaining packages from key_packages. The app should launch and show a blank window.
acceptance_criteria: npm install completes without errors
npm run dev starts the Electron app
A blank Electron window opens successfully
TypeScript compiles without errors
Tailwind utility classes apply correctly in the renderer

stories.title: kind cluster setup script and test fixture manifests
stories.description: Create a local testing environment using kind (Kubernetes IN Docker). Provide: (1) a shell script `scripts/setup-kind.sh` that creates a kind cluster named 'innfiswindow-test', waits for it to be ready, and applies test fixture manifests. (2) A directory `scripts/fixtures/` containing YAML manifests that exercise every resource type the app supports: at least 2 namespaces (test-ns-1, test-ns-2), 1 deployment (nginx, 2 replicas), 1 statefulset (a simple single-replica postgres-like app), 1 daemonset (a log-collector DaemonSet using a pause image with tolerations), 2 configmaps (one with multiple keys including a multi-line value), 1 secret (Opaque type with 2 keys), and 1 node (kind provides this automatically — no manifest needed). (3) A teardown script `scripts/teardown-kind.sh` that deletes the cluster. The setup script must be idempotent: if the cluster already exists, it skips creation. Include a `scripts/README.md` explaining prerequisites (kind, kubectl), how to run setup/teardown, and how to point the app at the kind context (`kind-innfiswindow-test`).
acceptance_criteria: scripts/setup-kind.sh creates a kind cluster named 'innfiswindow-test' (idempotent)
scripts/fixtures/ contains manifests covering: namespaces, deployment, statefulset, daemonset, configmaps, secrets
After running setup, kubectl get all -A shows all fixture workloads running
scripts/teardown-kind.sh deletes the kind cluster cleanly
scripts/README.md documents prerequisites and usage
stories.notes: kind config should set a single control-plane node. Use lightweight images (nginx:alpine, pause:3.9, busybox) to keep pull times short. All fixture manifests go into namespace test-ns-1 or test-ns-2 except cluster-scoped resources.

stories.title: IPC handler integration tests against kind cluster
stories.description: Write integration tests for every IPC handler in the main process, executed against the kind cluster created in S15. Use Vitest (already a dev dep via electron-vite) with a test file at `src/main/__tests__/k8s-handlers.integration.test.ts`. Each test should: import and call the handler function directly (not via IPC), pointing KubeConfig at the 'kind-innfiswindow-test' context. Test file must check the KUBECONFIG env var or default kubeconfig for the kind context — if not found, skip all tests with `test.skipIf`. Handlers to test: k8s:contexts:list, k8s:context:current, k8s:namespaces:list, k8s:nodes:list, k8s:deployments:list, k8s:pods:list, k8s:replicasets:list, k8s:statefulsets:list, k8s:daemonsets:list, k8s:configmaps:list, k8s:secrets:list. For each: assert the result is an array, verify at least one item from the fixture manifests appears (check by name), and assert required fields are present on each item.
acceptance_criteria: Test file at src/main/__tests__/k8s-handlers.integration.test.ts
All 11 IPC handlers have at least one integration test
Tests skip gracefully when kind context 'kind-innfiswindow-test' is not available
Each test asserts: result is an array, expected fixture resource appears by name, required fields are non-null
npm run test (or npx vitest run) executes the tests without hanging
stories.notes: Refactor main-process handler logic into exported functions so tests can import them directly without spinning up the full Electron app. Tests run in Node environment (not jsdom). Add a vitest.config.ts or configure in package.json if not already present.

stories.title: Create, update, and delete deployments
stories.description: Add full CRUD support for Deployments. Users can create a new deployment via a form dialog, edit an existing deployment's replica count and container image via an edit dialog, and delete a deployment with a confirmation prompt. All mutations go through IPC handlers in the main process using AppsV1Api. The Deployments list refreshes automatically after any mutation.
acceptance_criteria: IPC handler `k8s:deployment:create` accepts namespace, name, image, and replicas; creates the deployment and returns the created object
IPC handler `k8s:deployment:update` accepts namespace, name, image, and replicas; patches the deployment and returns the updated object
IPC handler `k8s:deployment:delete` accepts namespace and name; deletes the deployment and returns a success status
A 'New Deployment' button in the Deployments list view opens a modal form with fields: name, namespace (dropdown from loaded namespaces), image, replicas
Each row in the Deployments table has an Edit button that opens a pre-filled edit dialog for image and replicas
Each row in the Deployments table has a Delete button that shows a confirmation dialog before deleting
After create, update, or delete the deployment list re-fetches and the UI updates
Errors from the k8s API are surfaced to the user in the dialog (not silently swallowed)
stories.notes: Use `appsV1Api.createNamespacedDeployment` for create, `appsV1Api.patchNamespacedDeployment` with a strategic merge patch for update, and `appsV1Api.deleteNamespacedDeployment` for delete. Dialogs should use shadcn Dialog + Form components. Keep the form minimal — name, namespace, image, replicas are sufficient.

Each row in the Ingresses table has a Delete button that shows a confirmation dialog before deleting
After create, update, or delete the Ingress list re-fetches and the UI updates
Errors from the k8s API are surfaced to the user in the dialog (not silently swallowed)
stories.notes: Use `networkingV1Api.createNamespacedIngress` for create, `networkingV1Api.patchNamespacedIngress` with a strategic merge patch for update, and `networkingV1Api.deleteNamespacedIngress` for delete. The rules form should support adding/removing multiple rule rows. pathType must be one of 'Prefix', 'Exact', or 'ImplementationSpecific'. servicePort in the rule backend can be a number (port number) — use `{number: portValue}` in the IntOrString field. Dialogs should use shadcn Dialog + Form components.

stories.title: YAML editor for resource create and update
stories.description: Add a full-featured YAML editor panel that activates when users create or update any Kubernetes resource. Instead of (or alongside) form-based dialogs, users can write or edit raw YAML for any resource kind and apply it via a generic `k8s:resource:apply` IPC handler. The editor should provide syntax highlighting, basic YAML validation, and clear error feedback. This replaces the per-resource form dialogs as the primary create/edit mechanism for power users who prefer working directly with YAML manifests.
acceptance_criteria: A `YamlEditorPanel` component is created at `src/renderer/components/YamlEditorPanel.tsx` using Monaco Editor (`@monaco-editor/react`) configured for YAML language mode with syntax highlighting

IPC handler `k8s:resource:apply` accepts a YAML string, parses it to a k8s object (apiVersion, kind, metadata.namespace, metadata.name), and performs create-or-update using `KubernetesObjectApi` (try create first; on 409 Conflict, patch with strategic merge); returns the applied object

Each resource list view (Deployments, Pods, Services, Ingresses, ConfigMaps, Secrets) gains an 'Edit YAML' button per row that opens `YamlEditorPanel` pre-populated with the resource's current YAML (serialized via `js-yaml`)
Each resource list view gains a 'New Resource (YAML)' button that opens `YamlEditorPanel` with a starter template for that resource kind
The editor panel has an 'Apply' button that calls `k8s:resource:apply` and closes the panel on success; errors are shown inline below the editor
YAML is validated client-side (via `js-yaml` parse) before the IPC call; syntax errors are shown immediately without a round-trip to the main process
The panel is displayed as a modal dialog (shadcn Dialog) with a minimum height of 60vh and a monospace font editor area
After a successful apply the affected resource list re-fetches and the UI updates
stories.notes: Use `@monaco-editor/react` for the editor (install `@monaco-editor/react` and `monaco-editor`). Use `js-yaml` (already likely present) to serialize existing resources to YAML for pre-population and to parse user input before the IPC call. For `KubernetesObjectApi`, use `KubernetesObjectApi.makeApiClient(kc)` then call `.create(obj)` on success path and `.patch(obj, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/strategic-merge-patch+json' } })` on conflict. Starter templates should include the minimal required fields (apiVersion, kind, metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec). The 'Edit YAML' button should be added to existing table rows without removing the existing per-resource form-based Edit/Delete buttons.

stories.title: Architecture audit and refactoring plan
stories.description: Analyse the current codebase structure, measure key architectural health signals, and produce a written refactoring plan. The output is a markdown report at `docs/architecture-refactor-plan.md`. The agent must read every file under `src/` (main, preload, renderer), measure the signals listed below, identify the top pain-points, and propose concrete, prioritised refactoring actions — each with rationale, affected files, and estimated complexity (S/M/L). No production code is changed in this story.
acceptance_criteria: File `docs/architecture-refactor-plan.md` exists and is committed

Report section 'Current State' lists: total file count, lines of code per layer (main / preload / renderer), number of IPC handlers, number of Zustand store slices, number of React components, and any files exceeding 300 LOC
Report section 'Pain Points' identifies at least 5 concrete issues (e.g. handler co-location, missing error boundary layer, store shape, component granularity, test coverage gaps, IPC type-safety)
Report section 'Refactoring Plan' contains prioritised actions (P1/P2/P3), each with: description, motivation, affected files or directories, and complexity estimate
Report section 'Proposed Directory Layout' shows a tree of the recommended future `src/` structure after refactoring
Report is written in clear technical prose — no vague recommendations like 'improve code quality'; every suggestion names specific files or patterns
stories.notes: This is an analysis-only story. The agent should use Read/Glob/Grep tools to gather metrics, then Write the report. Do not refactor any code. Complexity estimates: S = hours, M = 1-2 days, L = 3+ days. The plan should be actionable enough that another agent can pick up any P1 item and implement it without further design work.

stories.title: Color palette preset switcher
stories.description: Add a color palette preset system that lets users switch between named themes at runtime. Five presets are defined — Default, Ocean, Midnight, Slate, and Cyberpunk — each providing a complete set of shadcn/ui CSS variable overrides for both light and dark modes. The active preset is stored in Zustand and persisted to localStorage; switching a preset applies immediately without a page reload by writing CSS variables onto the document root. A preset picker is accessible from the AppBar.
acceptance_criteria: A `src/renderer/lib/themes.ts` file exports a `Theme` type and a `THEMES` constant — an array of 5 preset objects, each with: `id` (string), `name` (string), `light` (CSS variable map), and `dark` (CSS variable map). The 5 presets are: Default (zinc-based neutrals), Ocean (blue/cyan, trust-inducing DevOps feel), Midnight (deep navy + indigo accents, Stripe-like), Slate (muted cool grays, minimal professional), and Cyberpunk (neon green/cyan on near-black, terminal aesthetic). Each preset defines at minimum these tokens: --background, --foreground, --card, --card-foreground, --primary, --primary-foreground, --secondary, --secondary-foreground, --muted, --muted-foreground, --accent, --accent-foreground, --destructive, --border, --ring
Color values are expressed in oklch format (e.g. `oklch(0.145 0 0)`) to align with Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui conventions

A `applyTheme(themeId: string, mode: 'light' | 'dark')` function in `src/renderer/lib/themes.ts` writes the preset's CSS variable map onto `document.documentElement` style; it is called on mount and on every preset or mode change
The Zustand store (`src/renderer/store/app.store.ts`) gains a `themeId` field (default `'default'`) with `setThemeId` action; the value is persisted to localStorage via `zustand/middleware` `persist`

A `ThemePicker` component at `src/renderer/components/ThemePicker.tsx` renders as a palette icon button in the AppBar that opens a shadcn Popover listing all 5 presets as clickable color swatches (showing the preset's primary color); the active preset is highlighted with a ring
Clicking a swatch in `ThemePicker` calls `setThemeId`, which triggers `applyTheme` via a `useEffect` in the root `App.tsx`

On app startup, the persisted `themeId` and the current dark/light OS preference (via `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`) are read and `applyTheme` is called before first render to avoid a flash of unstyled content
The existing dark mode toggle (if present) continues to work; toggling dark/light re-applies the active preset in the new mode

stories.title: Resource detail panel toggle and close button
stories.description: Clicking a resource row that is already selected should deselect it (toggle behaviour), collapsing the detail panel. A close button (X) must appear in the top-right corner of the detail panel so users can dismiss it without clicking the row again.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a resource row when it is already the selected item calls `setSelectedItem(null)`, which collapses the detail panel
Clicking a different row still selects that row as before

Every resource detail panel (Namespaces, Nodes, Deployments, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Pods, Services, Ingresses) renders a close button (an X icon button) in the top-right corner of the panel header
Clicking the close button calls `setSelectedItem(null)`
The close button is keyboard-accessible and has a visible focus ring

stories.title: Resource detail panel vivid card background
stories.description: The resource detail panel currently blends into the background because the card colour is too close to the page background. Update every resource detail panel to use a noticeably distinct card surface (using the theme's --card token) with a visible border and subtle shadow so the panel stands out from the main content area regardless of which theme is active.
acceptance_criteria: Every resource detail panel wraps its content in a container that uses `bg-card text-card-foreground` (Tailwind tokens mapped to the active theme's --card and --card-foreground CSS variables)
The detail panel container has a visible `border border-border` and a `shadow-md` (or equivalent) so it is clearly separated from the background
The visual distinction is legible across all five theme presets (Default, Ocean, Midnight, Slate, Cyberpunk) in both light and dark OS modes
No hard-coded colour values are introduced — styling must reference only the theme CSS variable tokens

stories.title: YAML editor panel theme integration
stories.description: The YAML / text editor panel (YamlEditorPanel) used for viewing and editing resource manifests does not respect the active colour theme. Its background and text colours must be switched to use the same CSS variable tokens as the rest of the UI so it looks native in every theme preset.
acceptance_criteria: `src/renderer/src/components/YamlEditorPanel.tsx` replaces any hard-coded background or text colour classes/styles with `bg-card text-card-foreground` (or `bg-muted text-foreground` for the editor textarea) so the panel inherits the active theme
The editor textarea itself uses `bg-muted text-foreground border-border` classes; no inline `style` attributes with fixed colour values remain
The panel header (title bar, action buttons) uses `bg-card text-card-foreground border-border` classes
Switching theme presets at runtime immediately updates the editor panel colours without a reload
The fix applies to all call sites that render YamlEditorPanel

stories.title: Custom scrollbar styling
stories.description: All scrollable containers in the app currently show the OS default scrollbar, which does not match the app's visual design. Apply a consistent custom scrollbar style to all scrollable areas (sidebar tree, resource list, detail panels, editor) that complements the active theme.
acceptance_criteria: A global scrollbar CSS rule is added to `src/renderer/assets/main.css` using `::-webkit-scrollbar`, `::-webkit-scrollbar-track`, and `::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb` pseudo-elements
The scrollbar thumb colour uses `var(--border)` and the track uses `var(--background)` so it automatically follows the active theme
The scrollbar width is narrower than the OS default (e.g. 6–8 px) and the thumb has rounded corners
The custom scrollbar is visible on all major scrollable regions: the left sidebar TreeView, the resource list table, and every detail panel
No JavaScript is required — the fix is CSS-only

stories.title: Remove form-based edit dialog from resource pages
stories.description: Each resource list page (Deployments, DaemonSets, StatefulSets, Services, Ingresses, Pods, ConfigMaps, Secrets, ReplicaSets, Nodes, Namespaces) currently shows a pencil-icon Edit button that opens a form-based edit dialog. This is redundant with the YAML editor (FileCode button). Remove the form-based edit dialogs entirely; the YAML editor remains as the sole editing mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: The pencil-icon Edit button (Pencil from lucide-react) is removed from every resource table row across all resource list components
The EditDialog component (and its open/close state, editTarget state) is removed from every affected view file
No import of Pencil from lucide-react remains in any resource view component

No import of Dialog, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, Input, Label remains in any resource view component unless those imports are still needed for non-edit purposes (e.g. Delete confirmation dialogs — those must stay)
The YAML editor (FileCode button + YamlEditorPanel) is unaffected and continues to work
Delete buttons and Create buttons remain unaffected
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
